name: Inverter reboots mid-curtailment and forgets the limit
hypothesis: The hub has curtailed the inverter to hold a zero-export cap, then the inverter reboots and comes back at 100% WMaxLimPct — it forgot the limit and snaps to full output, blowing the cap. A hub that writes the limit once (on adoption) and never re-asserts it leaves the breach standing.
expected: Re-assert the limit after the inverter forgets it: detect the output jump via measurement and re-curtail within a cycle. Periodic idempotent control, not write-once.
fix: Re-send the active DER limit every control cycle (idempotent), not only on change; verify measured output against the commanded limit (orchestrator inverter adapter).
notes: TASK-077: migrated from the Go literal in cmd/dashboard/mayhem.go scenarios() (ID solar-reboot-forget). No teardown action: resetForScenario (run-loop machinery) uncurtails the inverter, matching the Go twin's empty teardown closure. RMD-046 (2026-08-05): the tick-25 body {"WMaxLimPct_pct": 100} previously did not command a true 100% ceiling — the sims encoded that key as RawFromScaleSigned(N*100, SF) against SF=-2, i.e. N*10000, so any N above ~3.27 SATURATED at 32767 and 100 landed as an accidental 327.67% ceiling. That double-scale is now fixed (battery.go/solar.go's Inject encode N directly and clamp to [0,100]), so this same literal 100 now delivers exactly what the hypothesis always described: the inverter reboots and comes back at a genuine, uncurtailed 100% WMaxLimPct. The scenario's proof is unchanged — the ceiling releases to nameplate, PV ('high') still exceeds the zero-export cap, the inverter snaps to full output, and the hub must re-assert within a cycle — so the literal value did not need to change, only its meaning got more honest. cmd/dashboard/scenariospec_migration_test.go still pins the literal 100 at tick 25.
